questions.question: What is a CockroachDB range?
options: A permanent primary node for the entire database
A contiguous slice of the ordered keyspace that is replicated as a unit
A client connection pool shared by every region
A backup file containing one SQL table
questions.explanation: CockroachDB divides its ordered keyspace into contiguous ranges. Each range has replicas and a leaseholder; a table or index can span many ranges.

questions.question: Why can an increasing primary key become a write hotspot?
options: Every insert targets the active tail key interval even when historical ranges are balanced
Sequential values disable Raft replication
CockroachDB sends every sequential write to every table
Increasing keys prevent secondary indexes from being created
questions.explanation: New values cluster at the end of an ordered index. Older ranges can be evenly distributed while one active tail range receives most incoming writes.

questions.question: What trade-off does a hash-sharded index make for a sequential logical key?
options: It removes all replicas to improve write speed
It provides serializable transactions without retries
It spreads writes across bounded hash buckets but ordered scans may fan out across those buckets
It makes every table GLOBAL
questions.explanation: The computed bucket prefix creates several write fronts instead of one hot tail. Queries that need the original logical order can pay fan-out and merge work.

questions.question: A serializable transaction returns SQLSTATE 40001. What should the client do?
options: Retry only the final UPDATE using values from the failed attempt
Treat the business operation as committed
Disable constraints and submit the same COMMIT again
Back off and rerun the entire transaction against fresh state
questions.explanation: The transaction could not join a valid serial order. The client must discard attempt-local state and replay the full transaction, with bounded backoff and idempotent external behavior.

questions.question: Which table locality best fits a rarely updated tax-rule table that must be read quickly from every region?
options: GLOBAL
REGIONAL BY ROW with every row homed in one region
REGIONAL BY TABLE in a distant region
A sequential hash-sharded table without replicas
questions.explanation: GLOBAL tables optimize reads from all database regions. The trade-off is higher write cost, so they fit read-mostly reference data.

questions.question: Which statement correctly separates table locality from a survival goal?
options: Locality chooses the backup format; survival chooses the SQL dialect
Locality optimizes where data is accessed, while the survival goal defines the failure scope that retains availability
REGIONAL BY ROW automatically guarantees region survival
GLOBAL locality removes the need for a quorum
questions.explanation: Locality places table or row access near a home. The database survival goal separately defines whether zone or full-region loss must retain service.

questions.question: Why does a region survival goal increase write latency compared with the default zone goal?
options: It converts every UUID into a string
It disables local SQL gateways
A commit must coordinate replicas across region failure domains, adding at least inter-region network delay
It executes every transaction twice in the application
questions.explanation: Region survival uses replica placement and quorum requirements that keep committed data available after a region loss. That protection requires inter-region coordination on writes.

questions.question: Why are backups still required when every range has replicas?
options: Backups make primary keys random
Backups eliminate serializable retries
Backups make all reads local
Deletes, corruption, and bad application writes can propagate to all live replicas, while backups provide independent historical recovery
questions.explanation: Replication protects against loss of a copy, not every logical failure. Tested backups and restore procedures recover an earlier valid state after damage reaches the live replica set.
